tools.name: sandbox_create
tools.description: Creates an isolated spendctl sandbox and returns its sandbox_id. Call it first: every other tool needs the sandbox_id, and one sandbox serves a whole conversation (create another only to try a different preset). The sandbox is a real spendctl sidecar with a throwaway wallet, a mock x402 facilitator

tools.name: sandbox_pay
tools.description: Fetches one of the sandbox's paid endpoints (HTTP 402, x402) through the spendctl sidecar, which applies the sandbox agent's budget, allowlist and approval policy, pays with the throwaway wallet if allowed, and returns the response. tools.name: await_approval
tools.description: Waits for the decision on a payment that sandbox_pay reported as held, without paying again: long-polls the sandbox sidecar for up to timeoutSeconds (default 10, at most 20) and returns pending, approved, denied, expired or withdrawn, with the ledger entry and the decision deadline. tools.name: withdraw_approval
tools.description: Takes back a payment that sandbox_pay reported as held, as a real agent does when the task that needed the payment was cancelled or superseded: nothing is paid, the approval closes as withdrawn (distinct from deny), a later approve on that id is refused and await_approval answers withdrawn at once.

tools.name: check_budget
tools.description: Shows the sandbox agent's spending limits, what has been spent in each window and what is left. Use it before a paid call when the remaining budget matters, or after a refusal to see which limit was hit. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: sandbox_pay, list_receipts · Private data: sandbox_create, sandbox_pay, get_policy · Public sink: sandbox_create.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: sandbox_pay, list_receipts · Private data: sandbox_create, sandbox_pay, get_policy · Public sink: sandbox_create

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "sandbox_create" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
